setting.tex: Throughout the paper, we let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a \emph{separable metric space}, meaning that $\Xcal$ admits a countable \emph{dense} subset with respect to $\rho$. Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$ be a binary hypothesis class. For a hypothesis $h \in \Hcal$, let $\text{supp}(h) := \{x \in \Xcal: h(x) = 1\}$, that is, its collection of positive examples.
A generator is a map $\Gcal: \Xcal^{\star} \rightarrow \Xcal$ that takes a finite sequence of examples $x_1, x_2, \dots$ and outputs a new example $x$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$  be any hypothesis class satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property for some $r>0$ and let
$0< \vep_a, \vep_g \le r$. Then, $\Hcal$ is $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-uniformly generatable if and only if $\operatorname{C}_{ \vep_a, \vep_g} (\Hcal) < \infty$.

terms.tex:
Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$  be any hypothesis class satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property for some $r>0$ and let
$0<\vep_a,\vep_g \le r$. If there exists a generator $\Gcal$ and $d^{\star} \in \naturals$, such that for every $h \in \Hcal$ and any sequence $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(h)$, if there exists $t$ such that $N(\vep_a;\{x_i\}_{i=1}^t,\rho)\ge d^\star$, then $\Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in  \operatorname{supp}(h) \setminus  B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^s,\vep_g)$ for all $s \geq t$, then we say $\Hcal$ is \emph{($\vep_a,\vep_g$)-uniformly generatable}.

The \emph{$(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-closure dimension} of $\Hcal$, denoted
$\operatorname{C}_{\vep_a,\vep_g}(\Hcal)$, is the largest
$d\in\mathbb{N}$ such that there exist $h\in\Hcal$ and
$\{x_i\}_{i=1}^t\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(h)$ satisfying
\[
N(\vep_a;\{x_i\}_{i=1}^t,\rho)=d,
\]
and a finite set $F\subseteq\langle x_1,\dots,x_t\rangle_{\Hcal}$
such that
\[
\langle x_1,\dots,x_t\rangle_{\Hcal}\subseteq B(F,\vep_g).
\]
If this holds for arbitrarily large $d\in\mathbb{N}$, we set
$\operatorname{C}_{\vep_a,\vep_g}(\Hcal)=\infty$.
If no such sequence exists for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$, we set
$\operatorname{C}_{\vep_a,\vep_g}(\Hcal)=0$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$  be any finite hypothesis class satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property for some $r>0$ and let
$0< \vep_a, \vep_g \le r$ such that $\vep_g\le \vep_a$. Then, $\Hcal$ is $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-uniformly generatable.

Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a metric space and let $r>0$. A hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfies the \emph{$r$-Uniformly Unbounded Support ($r$-UUS)} property if every $h\in\Hcal$ has nonempty support and, for every sequence $(x_i)_{i\ge1}$ in $\operatorname{supp}(h)$ satisfying
     \[
     \operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{x_i:i\ge1\},r),
     \]
     we have
     \[
     \lim_{t\to\infty}N(r;\{x_1,\dots,x_t\},\rho)=\infty.
     \]

quotes.tex: Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a doubling metric space. Suppose $\Hcal \subseteq \{0,1\}^\Xcal$ is a class satisfying $r$-UUS property for some $r > 0$. Then it also satisfies the $r'$-UUS property for any $r' > 0$. In this case, we simply say that $\Hcal$ has the UUS property.

terms.tex:
Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a metric space and let $r>0$. A hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfies the \emph{$r$-Uniformly Unbounded Support ($r$-UUS)} property if every $h\in\Hcal$ has nonempty support and, for every sequence $(x_i)_{i\ge1}$ in $\operatorname{supp}(h)$ satisfying
     \[
     \operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{x_i:i\ge1\},r),
     \]
     we have
     \[
     \lim_{t\to\infty}N(r;\{x_1,\dots,x_t\},\rho)=\infty.
     \]

A metric space $(\Xcal,\rho)$ is said to be \emph{doubling} if there exists a constant $M>0$ such that for any $x\in\Xcal$ and any $r>0$, the ball $ B(x,r)$
can be covered by at most $M$ balls of radius $r/2$.

quotes.tex:
Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a doubling metric space.  
Let $\vep_a,\vep_g,\delta_a,\delta_g>0$ satisfy $0<\delta_a<\vep_a$ and $0<\delta_g<\vep_g$. 
Suppose $\Hcal\subseteq \{0,1\}^\Xcal$ satisfies the UUS property. 
Then $\Hcal$ is $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-uniformly (resp.\ non-uniformly) generatable if and only if it is $(\delta_a,\delta_g)$-uniformly (resp.\ non-uniformly) generatable.

quotes.tex: Let $(\Xcal,\rho_1)$ be a doubling metric space, and let $\rho_2$ be a metric on $\Xcal$ bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\rho_1$. Suppose $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^\Xcal$ is a hypothesis class. Then, it satisfies the UUS property with respect to $\rho_1$ if and only if it satisfies the UUS property with respect to $\rho_2$. If these equivalent UUS conditions hold, then $\Hcal$ is uniformly (resp.\ non-uniformly) generatable with respect to $\rho_1$ if and only if it is uniformly (resp.\ non-uniformly) generatable with respect to $\rho_2$.

can be covered by at most $M$ balls of radius $r/2$.

Let $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ be two metrics on the same space $\Xcal$.
We say that $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are \emph{equivalent} if there exist
constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ such that for all $x,y\in\Xcal$,
\[
    c\,\rho_1(x,y) \le \rho_2(x,y) \le C\,\rho_1(x,y).
\]

     \[

     \]
     we have
     \[
     \lim_{t\to\infty}N(r;\{x_1,\dots,x_t\},\rho)=\infty.
     \]

quotes.tex: On the real line $\mathbb R$, there is a hypothesis class $\Hcal$ that satisfies the UUS property, and is $(\vep,1)$-generatable in the limit for any $\vep\in(0,1)$, but not $(1,1)$-generatable in the limit.

quotes.tex:
In $\ell^2$-space, for any $r>0$ and any
$0<\vep_{a1}\le \vep_{a2}\le r$ and $0<\vep_g\le r$,
there exists a hypothesis class $\Hcal \subseteq \{0,1\}^{\ell^2}$
satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property with the following
generation behavior. For $\gamma_g\in(0,\vep_g)$,
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\gamma_a\in[\vep_{a2},r],
& \text{then $(\gamma_a,\gamma_g)$-uniformly generatable},\\[1mm]
\gamma_a\in[\vep_{a1},\vep_{a2}),
& \text{then $(\gamma_a,\gamma_g)$-non-uniformly but not uniformly generatable},\\[1mm]
\gamma_a\in(0,\vep_{a1}),
&  \text{then $(\gamma_a,\gamma_g)$-generatable in the limit but not non-uniformly generatable}.
\end{array}
\]
Moreover, for $\gamma_g\in[\vep_g,r]$ and any $\gamma_a\in(0,r]$,
$\Hcal$ is not $(\gamma_a,\gamma_g)$-generatable in the limit.

If there exists a generator $\Gcal$ such that for every $h \in \Hcal$, and any sequence $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty\subseteq \operatorname{supp}(h)$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty,\vep_a)$ (i.e., the adversary eventually reveals an $\vep_a$-cover of the support), there exists a  $t^{\star} \in \naturals$ such  that $\Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in \operatorname{supp}(h) \setminus  B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^s,\vep_g)$ for all $s \geq t^{\star}$, then we say $\Hcal$ is \emph{($\vep_a,\vep_g$)-generatable in the limit}.

quotes.tex: Let $\Xcal$ be a metric space with metric $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$. Assume there exists $M>0$ such that for any $x, y\in \Xcal$, $ \rho_2(x,y)\le M\rho_1(x,y)$. Let $\Hcal\subseteq \{0,1\}^\Xcal$ be any class satisfying the $r$-UUS property for an $r>0$ with respect to $\rho_2$, and $0<\vep_a,\vep_g\le r$. Then $\Hcal$ satisfies the $r/M$-UUS property with respect to $\rho_1$. Moreover, if $\Hcal$ is $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-generatable in the limit with respect to $\rho_2$, then $\Hcal$ is also $(\vep_a/M,\vep_g/M)$-generatable in the limit with respect to $\rho_1$.

terms.tex:
Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a metric space and let $r>0$. A hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfies the \emph{$r$-Uniformly Unbounded Support ($r$-UUS)} property if every $h\in\Hcal$ has nonempty support and, for every sequence $(x_i)_{i\ge1}$ in $\operatorname{supp}(h)$ satisfying
     \[
     \operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{x_i:i\ge1\},r),
     \]
     we have
     \[
     \lim_{t\to\infty}N(r;\{x_1,\dots,x_t\},\rho)=\infty.
     \]

Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$  be any hypothesis class satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property for some $r>0$ and let
$0<\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_g \le r$. If there exists a generator $\Gcal$ such that for every $h \in \Hcal$, and any sequence $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty\subseteq \operatorname{supp}(h)$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty,\vep_a)$ (i.e., the adversary eventually reveals an $\vep_a$-cover of the support), there exists a  $t^{\star} \in \naturals$ such  that $\Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in \operatorname{supp}(h) \setminus  B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^s,\vep_g)$ for all $s \geq t^{\star}$, then we say $\Hcal$ is \emph{($\vep_a,\vep_g$)-generatable in the limit}.

quotes.tex:
Let $\Xcal$ be a countable set equipped with the discrete metric
\[
\rho(x,y)=
\begin{cases}
1, & x\neq y,\\
0, & x=y.
\end{cases}
\]
Let $r<1$ and $0<\vep_a,\vep_g\le r$. Suppose $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfies the $r$-UUS property.
Then $\Hcal$ is $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-generatable in the limit (respectively, $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-non-uniformly generatable, $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-uniformly generatable) if and only if $\Hcal$ is generatable in the limit (respectively, non-uniformly generatable, uniformly generatable) in the sense of \cite{li2024generationlenslearningtheory} (see Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_countable} for the definitions).

terms.tex:
The hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq{\{0,1\}}^\Xcal$ is \emph{generatable in the limit} if there exists a generator $\Gcal$ such that for every $h \in \Hcal$ and every enumeration $\{x_1,x_2,\dots\}$ of $\operatorname{supp}(h)$, there exists $t^\star \in \naturals$ such that $\Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in \operatorname{supp}(h)\setminus \{x_1,\dots,x_s\}
\quad$ for all $s \ge t^\star.$

The hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq{\{0,1\}^\Xcal}$ is \emph{non-uniformly generatable} if there exists a generator $\Gcal$ such that for every $h \in \Hcal$, there exists an integer $d_h^\star \in \naturals$ such that for every sequence $\{x_1,x_2,\dots\} \subseteq \operatorname{supp}(h)$, if there exists $t\in\naturals$ such that $|\{x_1,\dots,x_t\}|=d_h^\star$, then $ \Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in \operatorname{supp}(h)\setminus \{x_1,\dots,x_s\} \quad \text{for all } s \ge t.$

quotes.tex:
Let $\Hcal$ satisfy $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ and let $0<\vep_a,\vep_g\le r$. Let $\mathcal S$ be a family of nonempty subsets of $\Xcal$, and let $T_1,\dots,T_q\subseteq\Xcal$ satisfy $\bigcap_{i=1}^qT_i=\emptyset$. Suppose that, for every $S\in\mathcal S$ and $i\in[q]$, $\Hcal$ contains a hypothesis $h_{S,i}$ with support $S\cup T_i$. If $\Gcal$ is an $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-non-uniform generator for $\Hcal$, then for every $S\in\mathcal S$ there is a finite threshold $d_S$ such that, for every sequence $(x_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $S$, whenever
\[
N(\vep_a;\{x_1,\dots,x_t\},\rho)\ge d_S,
\]
we have
\[
\Gcal(x_{1:s})\in S\setminus B(\{x_1,\dots,x_s\},\vep_g)
\qquad\text{for every }s\ge t.
\]

Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0, 1\}^{\Xcal}$ be any hypothesis class satisfying the $r$-$\operatorname{UUS}$ property for some $r>0$ and let
$0<\vep_a,\vep_g \le r$. If there exists a generator $\Gcal$ such that for every $h \in \Hcal$ there exists a $d_h\in\naturals$, such that for any sequence $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^\infty\subseteq \operatorname{supp}(h)$, if there exists~$t$ such that $N(\vep_a;\{x_i\}_{i=1}^t,\rho)\ge d_h$, then $\Gcal(x_{1:s}) \in  \operatorname{supp}(h) \setminus  B(\{x_i\}_{i=1}^s,\vep_g)$ for all $s \geq t$, then we say $\Hcal$ is \emph{($\vep_a,\vep_g$)-non-uniformly generatable}.

Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a metric space and $\vep>0$.  
    An $\vep$-covering of a set $A\subseteq \Xcal$ is a finite set $\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_M\}\subset \Xcal$ such that
    $A\subset B(\{\theta_i\}_{i=1}^M,\vep)$. The $\vep$-covering number $N(\vep;A,\rho)$ is defined as
    \[
        N(\vep;A,\rho)
        :=
        \min\left\{M\in\mathbb N:\exists\ \vep\text{-covering of }A \text{ with }M\text{ points}\right\}.
    \]
    If no such finite covering exists, we write $N(\vep;A,\rho)=\infty$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\Hcal \subseteq \{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfy the $r$-UUS property for some $r>0$, and let
$0<\vep_a,\vep_g\le r$.
Suppose there exist $k\in \mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, points $y_1,\dots,y_k\in \Xcal$,
a sequence $(x_{0i})_{i\ge 1}\subseteq \Xcal$, and an array $(x_{ij})_{i\ge 1,\,j\ge 1}\subseteq \Xcal$
such that the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a set $A_0\subseteq \Xcal$ such that for every infinite sequence of positive
integers $(j_i)_{i\ge 1}$, there exists $h\in\Hcal$ containing all the specified observations:
\[
\{y_\ell:1\le\ell\le k\}\cup\{x_{0i}:i\ge1\}
\cup\bigcup_{i\ge1}\{x_{i\ell}:1\le\ell\le j_i\}
\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(h),
\]
and satisfying
\[
\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{y_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^k,\vep_a)\ \cup\ B(\{x_{0i}\}_{i\ge 1},\vep_a)\ \cup\
B\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\ge 1}\{x_{i\ell}:\,1\le \ell\le j_i\},\,\vep_a\Bigr),
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{y_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^k,\vep_g)\ \cup\ A_0\ \cup\
B\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\ge 1}\{x_{i\ell}:\,1\le \ell\le j_i\},\,\vep_g\Bigr).
\]

\item For every $n\ge 1$, there exists a set $A_n\subseteq \Xcal$ such that for every finite sequence
of positive integers $(j_i)_{i=0}^{n-1}$, there exists $h\in\Hcal$ containing all the specified observations:
\[
\{y_\ell:1\le\ell\le k\}\cup\{x_{ni}:i\ge1\}
\cup\bigcup_{i=0}^{n-1}\{x_{i\ell}:1\le\ell\le j_i\}
\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(h),
\]
and satisfying
\[
\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{y_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^k,\vep_a)\ \cup\ B(\{x_{ni}\}_{i\ge 1},\vep_a)\ \cup\
B\Bigl(\bigcup_{i=0}^{n-1}\{x_{i\ell}:\,1\le \ell\le j_i\},\,\vep_a\Bigr),
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{supp}(h)\subseteq B(\{y_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^k,\vep_g)\ \cup\ A_n\ \cup\
B\Bigl(\bigcup_{i=0}^{n-1}\{x_{i\ell}:\,1\le \ell\le j_i\},\,\vep_g\Bigr).
\]

\item For every $n\ge 1$,
\[
A_n\ \cap\ \Bigl(A_0 \ \cup\ B(\{x_{ij}\}_{i\ge n+1,\ j\ge 1},\vep_g)\Bigr)\ =\ \emptyset.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Hcal$ is not $(\vep_a,\vep_g)$-generatable in the limit.

Let $(\Xcal,\rho)$ be a metric space and let $r>0$. A hypothesis class $\Hcal\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\Xcal}$ satisfies the \emph{$r$-Uniformly Unbounded Support ($r$-UUS)} property if every $h\in\Hcal$ has nonempty support and, for every sequence $(x_i)_{i\ge1}$ in $\operatorname{supp}(h)$ satisfying
     \[
